title: Fee Recognition Note — Tank Ownership and the Fees That Enter a Plan Year
content:
Whether the fees billed on an account under Refined Fuels and Propane Accounts enter the plan year's cost depends on whose tank stands at the site and, where it is the cooperative's, on how much fuel the account took over the plan year.

1. **Where the tank is the cooperative's and the gallons taken over the plan year reach the programme's waiver gallons**, none of the fees billed is recognised.
2. **Where the tank is the cooperative's and the gallons taken over the plan year fall under the programme's waiver gallons**, half of the fees billed is recognised, the share standing at 0.5.
3. **Where the tank is the member's own**, the whole of the fees billed is recognised, whatever the gallons taken.

## Points of judgement

**Which gallons are counted.** The gallons delivered on the account over the plan year, measured against the waiver gallons the catalogue writes for the programme the account sits on. The test is reached at the waiver figure exactly.

**Whose tank it is.** The tank recorded on the account. On a cooperative tank the first two lines apply; on a member's own tank the third applies and the gallons do not enter the judgement at all.

*Hypothetical, on a cooperative tank.* An account on a programme whose waiver gallons stand at 400 takes 400.0 gallons over the plan year. The waiver figure is reached, so none of the 260.00 USD of fees billed enters the year's cost. Had the account taken 399.0 gallons, half of the fees would be recognised and 130.00 USD would enter the year's cost.

*Hypothetical, on a member's own tank.* An account whose tank is the member's own takes 399.0 gallons over the plan year. The whole 260.00 USD of fees billed enters the year's cost.
